image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Rock Beauty fish (Holocanthus tricolor). The image captures the anterior to mid-section of the fish, showing the characteristic black head and front body transitioning into a bright yellow posterior. The eye is visible on the left edge, and the dorsal and anal fins are partially visible with blue margins.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible curvature of the dorsal and ventral profiles indicates a deep, laterally compressed body typical of angelfish/butterflyfish.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the diagnostic black anterior hood and bright yellow posterior body. A dark margin is visible on the dorsal fin edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is visible along the top edge, appearing continuous. While individual rays are hard to distinguish due to resolution, the structure is intact.
The anal fin is visible on the bottom edge, mirroring the dorsal fin's position and general shape.
The caudal peduncle and tail are outside the frame or heavily blurred in the background; cannot be verified.

The background dissolves into an indistinct smear rather than a natural bokeh, and the transition to the tail area is unnaturally abrupt/blurry, potentially indicating inpainting or generation boundary issues.
